McLaren: McLaren has fitted a brand‑new, low‑downforce rear wing that’s been tuned specifically for this circuit’s fast, flowing corners. The revised wing reduces drag, letting the car carry more speed down the straights while still staying stable in the high‑speed turns. In short, it should give McLaren a better balance between straight‑line pace and corner‑holding, which could make a real difference in qualifying and the race.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has tweaked the rear of the car – re‑shaping the suspension and the little wing‑lets at the rear corners – to give the car a more stable, predictable feel when it’s on the edge of grip. They’ve also adjusted the rear‑wing flap to suit this circuit’s balance between straight‑line speed and cornering down‑force, meaning the team should be able to pull harder out of the bends without sacrificing top‑end pace. In short, the changes should make the car feel tighter in the corners and give Ferrari a better shot at defending and attacking this weekend.
Racing Bulls / RB: Racing Bulls has tweaked the front wing’s outer sections and added extra camber to the front‑suspension wishbones, giving the car a bit more front‑end grip as the weekend’s high‑downforce layout demands better turn‑in. The side‑pod inlet has been merged into a wider single opening, prompting a reshaped engine cover and rear‑corner winglets to keep airflow smooth and improve rear stability, while a new rear‑wing profile trims drag for the long straights. Altogether, these aero clean‑ups should boost corner speed and keep the car stable through the fast sections, giving RB a stronger shot at the podium.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has tweaked the front wing by extending the outermost element, which smooths the airflow around the car’s front end and gives a little extra grip into the corners. At the rear, they’ve shifted the drum‑lip section of the rear corner inwards, helping the tyre load stay more consistent and improving stability under braking. Together, these changes should make the car feel more balanced and allow the drivers to push harder, especially through the high‑speed turns of this weekend’s circuit.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin has trimmed the front‑wing flaps and shortened the nose, giving the car a tighter, more agile front end that will help it turn quicker on this circuit’s twisty sections. The rear wing has been made smaller and the beam wing reduced to a single element, cutting drag so the car can keep higher straight‑line speed. Together, these changes should make the AMR‑24 more balanced through the corners while still preserving the power needed for a strong qualifying and race performance this weekend.
Alpine F1 Team: Alpine has fitted a low‑downforce rear wing and a matching low‑downforce beam wing, tuned specifically for this circuit’s high‑speed sections. The slimmer, drag‑focused setup will let the car carry more straight‑line speed, helping it hit higher top‑ends on the long straights. In short, the change aims to boost straight‑line pace without sacrificing the grip needed through the corners, giving Alpine a better shot at overtaking and a stronger overall lap this weekend.

Williams Racing: Williams has tweaked the shape of its forward floor fences and the rear floor edge wing/spat, plus refined the side‑pod inlet and engine cover openings, to smooth the air flowing under and around the car. These subtle reshapes should give a cleaner aerodynamic pack, boosting downforce and stability without adding drag – exactly the kind of extra grip the team hopes will translate into stronger qualifying laps and better cornering this weekend.
